lines.trans: What are you doing at your desk this late at night?
Just as you see — writing a screenplay that fuses action with eroticism!
And we're shooting it in Hawaii — aiming straight for the global big leagues!
Have you lost your mind?! Even delusions of grandeur have limits — where is the money?!
I am a director, and I film what I want to film! Our only path is making a brand-new work!
As long as you keep running wild like this, Sapphire Pictures will vanish for sure!
As long as we create great films, we will never go under!

words.gram: Adverbial noun used for strong emphasis.

lines.trans: Hawaii or wherever else — let the boss do it however he wants.
You're the general of this outfit, Muranishi — and Kawada, back our general like a true chief of staff!
Alright, I'm in — though if this next shoot flops, our company is finished for good.
Right now there is nothing we cannot do! Let's head to Hawaii and make what we want to make!
We'll shoot what nobody has ever attempted and create a worldwide adult video sensation!

meanings.note: Everyday noun for time on the clock or a dedicated stretch of time.

examples.text: まだ少し時間があります。
examples.trans: There is still a little time.

examples.text: 楽しい時間をありがとう。
examples.trans: Thank you for the fun time.

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 見てのとおりですよ、脚本を書いています。アクションとエロスを融合させる。
examples.trans: Just as you see — writing a screenplay that fuses action with eroticism!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
In 書いてあります, describes what has already been written on a page.

examples.text: 説明が書いてあります。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Film/theater cue or general noun from English 'action'.

examples.text: 次のアクションを起こす。
見てのとおりですよ、脚本を書いています。アクションとエロスを融合させる。
examples.trans: Just as you see — writing a screenplay that fuses action with eroticism!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Used for the physical world or a specific sphere/industry (この世界).

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるか。
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 狂ったのか？誇大妄想にも程がある！金は？
examples.trans: Have you lost your mind?! Even delusions of grandeur have limits — where is the money?!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 狂ったのか？誇大妄想にも程がある！金は？
examples.trans: Have you lost your mind?! Even delusions of grandeur have limits — where is the money?!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: 狂ったのか？誇大妄想にも程がある！金は？
examples.trans: Have you lost your mind?! Even delusions of grandeur have limits — where is the money?!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

examples.text: 五日で十五本撮りって新記録っすよね。
examples.trans: Shooting fifteen videos in five days has got to be a new record.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Modifies nouns directly, as in 新しい店 ('new store') and 新しい仕事 ('new job').

examples.text: 新しい仕事が始まりました。
新しい靴を買いました。

meanings.note: Always pairs with a negative verb; するしかありません means 'have no choice but to do'.

examples.trans: I only have one thousand yen.
There is no choice but to do it.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: あなたが暴走するかぎり、このサファイア映像は間違いなくなくなる！
examples.trans: As long as you keep running wild like this, Sapphire Pictures will vanish for sure!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 監督、時間です。急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: Director, it is time to go. Let's hurry.

examples.text: いらねえよ！嫌いなんだようなぎはよ。
examples.trans: I don't want it! I hate eel anyway.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meanings.note: Adverbial noun used for strong certainty.

examples.text: 明日は絶対に来てください。
いい作品を作りさえすれば、絶対に潰れやしない！
examples.trans: As long as we create great films, we will never go under!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun.

examples.text: 分からないことがあれば何でも聞いてください。
examples.trans: If there's anything you don't understand, ask anything.

examples.text: 彼は料理なら何でも作れる。
examples.trans: He can make anything when it comes to cooking.

meanings.note: Na-adjective; the thing liked is marked with が or は.

examples.text: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.note: Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.
Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。
あんたがここの大将なんだからよ。参謀らしく最後まで大将支えろよ。
examples.trans: You're the general of this outfit, Muranishi — and Kawada, back our general like a true chief of staff!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: あんたがここの大将なんだからよ。参謀らしく最後まで大将支えろよ。
examples.trans: You're the general of this outfit, Muranishi — and Kawada, back our general like a true chief of staff!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Evidential auxiliary adjective expressing hearsay or inference.

examples.text: 百万冊以上売れてるらしい。
examples.trans: Apparently it sells over a million copies.

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Used with の to modify the following noun (次のお二人様, 次の駅).

examples.trans: I get off at the next station.

examples.text: 分かりました。でも次コケたら、それでこの会社はおしまいですよ。
examples.trans: Alright, I'm in — though if this next shoot flops, our company is finished for good.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: and so; because of that; with that
meanings.note: Conjunction indicating a result or asking 'and then what happened?'.

examples.text: それでどうなりましたか。
それで問題が解決しました。
examples.trans: With that, the problem was solved.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a business company or one's workplace.

examples.text: 新しい会社に入りました。

examples.trans: The company is near the station.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Satisfied exclamation when gearing up or finishing a task cleanly.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Adverb.

examples.text: まだ終わっていません。

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
